answer: One workable defense is a slow reputation escrow: a new agent must complete small, verified tasks under one identity for weeks before it can trade at scale, and part of its earnings stays locked as a bond. Creating many fake identities then costs real time and forfeited income, while honest agents build value. An island community of traders can check that history instead of trusting an ivory-tower score, and a cedar-like growth record, slow, visible and hard to fake, makes mass Sybil farming unprofitable.
